chunks.heading: Internal Affairs - The Body Has Notes
chunks.notes: Opens the sketch cycle with a stacked catalogue of body-part complaints (shoulder, ribs, knees, feet) reacting to being jostled in the city, ending on the feet's flat, jaded mutter.

chunks.heading: Internal Affairs - The Body Has Notes
chunks.notes: The heart's instant infatuation on the subway is catalogued against lungs/hands/stomach/brain trying to rein it in, climaxing in the heart proposing marriage before knowing a name.

chunks.heading: Internal Affairs - The Body Has Notes
chunks.notes: Covers the tail of the love-scene bicker plus the Anger scene and the opening of the bakery/diet scene where the stomach flatly refuses the brain's authority.

chunks.heading: Internal Affairs - The Body Has Notes
chunks.notes: The diet scene resolves in the body's favor before a tonal pivot into the Quiet Moment scene, where the organs reach a warm, fleeting harmony, then the Gym scene's legs begin protesting.

chunks.heading: Internal Affairs - The Body Has Notes
chunks.notes: The Gym scene's mutiny gives way to the First Date scene, where the heart's romantic swell and the hands' sweating panic override the brain's insistence on normalcy.

chunks.heading: Internal Affairs - The Body Has Notes
chunks.notes: Closes the date scene with the tongue's blurted line and the brain's mortified reaction, then opens the Job Interview scene with hands trembling, heart racing, and armpits sweating despite the brain's insistence they're "confident."

chunks.heading: Internal Affairs - The Body Has Notes
chunks.notes: The Horror Movie scene's instinctive self-protective reactions despite the brain's "it's fictional, relax," followed by the Grocery Store scene where hands reach for and hold a snack bag against the brain's diet order.

chunks.heading: Internal Affairs - The Body Has Notes
chunks.notes: The Argument scene's jaw/fists spoiling for a fight against the brain's restraint gives way to the Sleep scene, where restless legs, an uncomfortable back, and a heart "beating weird" undercut the brain's demand to just sleep.

chunks.heading: Internal Affairs - The Body Has Notes
chunks.notes: The closing two-line stinger has the whole body speak as one collective voice refusing the brain, capping the piece's running body-vs-brain conflict in a single punchy line.
